title: Using Special Tests Wisely — Rule In, Rule Out and Clusters

hook.en: A positive test does not prove a diagnosis and a negative one does not clear it. Learn how a test changes the odds, and why clusters beat single tests.
hook.ur: Positive test diagnosis sabit nahi karta aur negative test use clear nahi karta. Seekhein ke test chance ko kaise badalta hai, aur clusters ek akele test se behtar kyun hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll use sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios to judge a test, work out a post-test probability, and build a small cluster for a clinical question.
goal.ur: End tak aap sensitivity, specificity aur likelihood ratios se test ka andaza lagayenge, post-test probability nikalenge, aur clinical sawal ke liye chhota cluster banayenge.

text.en: Every special test is a **question with an uncertain answer**. **Sensitivity** is how often the test is positive when the person has the problem; **specificity** is how often it is negative when they do not. A very sensitive test, when negative, helps to **rule out** (SnNout). A very specific test, when positive, helps to **rule in** (SpPin). But what you really need is how much a result **moves the odds**, and that is the **likelihood ratio**.
text.ur: Har special test ek **ghair-yaqeeni jawab wala sawal** hai. **Sensitivity** yeh hai ke masle wale logon mein test kitni baar positive aata hai; **specificity** yeh hai ke masle ke baghair logon mein kitni baar negative aata hai. Bohat sensitive test negative ho to **rule out** karne mein madad deta hai (SnNout). Bohat specific test positive ho to **rule in** karne mein madad deta hai (SpPin). Lekin asal mein aap ko yeh chahiye ke result chance ko **kitna badalta hai**, aur yeh **likelihood ratio** batata hai.

text.en: Think of a weather forecast. Before you look outside, you already guess a 30% chance of rain from the season and the sky. A positive test is like seeing dark clouds: the chance goes up a lot. A negative test is like seeing clear sky: the chance goes down. How much it moves depends on how good the forecast is, and where you started.
text.ur: Mausam ki forecast ki tarah sochein. Bahar dekhne se pehle hi mausam aur aasmaan se aap 30% baarish ka andaza lagate hain. Positive test kaale baadal dekhne jaisa hai: chance bohat barh jata hai. Negative test saaf aasmaan dekhne jaisa hai: chance ghat jata hai. Kitna badalta hai yeh forecast ki acchai aur aap ke shuruaati andaze par munhasir hai.

title.en: From a test result to a probability
title.ur: Test ke result se probability tak

steps.title: Start with a pre-test probability
steps.detail: Use the history and the setting: how likely is this problem before the test? A young footballer with a twisting injury and swelling has a high chance of an ACL tear. || Pre-test probability se shuru karein

steps.title: Pick the likelihood ratio
steps.detail: A positive LR above about 5 raises the odds a lot; a negative LR below about 0.2 lowers them a lot. Values near 1 change almost nothing. || Likelihood ratio chunein

steps.title: Multiply the odds
steps.detail: Convert the probability to odds, multiply by the LR, then convert back. For example, 30% becomes odds of 0.43; times an LR of 6 gives 2.6, which is about 72%. || Odds ko multiply karein

steps.title: Combine tests, then decide
steps.detail: One test moves the odds a little; several that agree move them much more. Decide whether the new probability is high enough to act, or whether you need more information. || Tests ko milayein, phir faisla karein

question.en: A test has a positive LR of 1.2. What does a positive result do?
question.ur: Ek test ka positive LR 1.2 hai. Positive result kya karta hai?

text.en: Almost nothing: it barely changes the odds
text.ur: Taqreeban kuch nahi: yeh chance ko mushkil se badalta hai

feedback.en: Yes — an LR close to 1 is nearly useless for changing a decision.
feedback.ur: Haan — 1 ke qareeb LR faisla badalne ke liye taqreeban bekaar hai.

feedback.en: A positive result cannot rule out a problem.
feedback.ur: Positive result masle ko rule out nahi kar sakta.

feedback.en: Only a large LR does that.
feedback.ur: Sirf bara LR aisa karta hai.

title.ur: Kaun sa test kis kaam ke liye?

rows.ur: "Kya main ise mehfooz tareeqay se rule out kar sakta hoon?"

rows.en: A negative result misses few true cases
rows.ur: Negative result se kam asli cases miss hote hain

rows.en: "Am I sure enough to treat or refer?"
rows.ur: "Kya mujhe ilaaj ya refer karne ka yaqeen hai?"

rows.en: A positive result rarely occurs without the problem
rows.ur: Positive result masle ke baghair kam aata hai

rows.en: A decision rule such as the Ottawa rules
It is built to avoid missing fractures
rows.ur: Yeh fractures miss na karne ke liye bani hai

text.en: **SnNout and SpPin.** A negative on a Sensitive test rules OUT; a positive on a Specific test rules IN. But always check how big the likelihood ratio is.
text.ur: **SnNout aur SpPin.** Sensitive test par negative OUT karta hai; Specific test par positive IN karta hai. Lekin hamesha dekhein ke likelihood ratio kitna bara hai.

text.en: **Using one test to decide.** A single test with a middling accuracy leaves a lot of doubt. A positive Hawkins-Kennedy test alone does not mean subacromial pain, and a negative McMurray does not clear the meniscus. Always combine the result with the history and other tests.
text.ur: **Ek test se faisla karna.** Darmiyani accuracy wala akela test bohat shak chhor deta hai. Akela positive Hawkins-Kennedy subacromial dard ka matlab nahi, aur negative McMurray meniscus clear nahi karta. Result ko hamesha history aur doosre tests ke saath milayein.

question.en: The pre-test chance is 30% and a test has a negative LR of 0.2. About what is the chance after a negative result?
question.ur: Pre-test chance 30% hai aur test ka negative LR 0.2 hai. Negative result ke baad chance takriban kitna hai?

feedback.en: A good negative LR lowers the chance.
feedback.ur: Acha negative LR chance ghatata hai.

feedback.en: A negative result lowers, not raises.
feedback.ur: Negative result ghatata hai, barhata nahi.

feedback.en: Yes — odds of 0.43 times 0.2 is about 0.086, which is about 8%.
feedback.ur: Haan — 0.43 odds ko 0.2 se multiply karne par takriban 0.086 aata hai, jo takriban 8% hai.

question.en: You need to be confident enough to rule a condition out. Which kind of test result helps most?
question.ur: Aap ko kisi bimari ko rule out karne ke liye kaafi yaqeen chahiye. Kaun sa test result sab se zyada madad karta hai?

text.en: A negative result on a highly sensitive test
text.ur: Bohat sensitive test par negative result

feedback.en: Yes — a very sensitive test misses few true cases, so a negative result is reassuring (SnNout).
feedback.ur: Haan — bohat sensitive test asli cases kam miss karta hai, is liye negative result tasalli bakhsh hai (SnNout).

text.en: A positive result on a highly specific test
text.ur: Bohat specific test par positive result

feedback.en: That helps to rule IN, not out.
feedback.ur: Yeh rule IN mein madad karta hai, out mein nahi.

text.en: A negative result on a test with a negative LR near 1
text.ur: Aisay test par negative result jis ka negative LR 1 ke qareeb ho

feedback.en: An LR near 1 barely changes the odds.
feedback.ur: 1 ke qareeb LR chance ko mushkil se badalta hai.

text.en: **Build a small cluster for a question.** For subacromial pain: painful arc, pain or weakness on resisted external rotation and a positive Hawkins-Kennedy. For ACL: history of a twist and swelling, a positive Lachman and a positive pivot shift. For fracture risk: use a decision rule rather than a single test.
text.ur: **Sawal ke liye chhota cluster banayein.** Subacromial dard ke liye: painful arc, resisted external rotation par dard ya kamzori aur positive Hawkins-Kennedy. ACL ke liye: twist aur sujan ki history, positive Lachman aur positive pivot shift. Fracture risk ke liye ek test ke bajaye decision rule istemal karein.

question.en: Why can the same test be more accurate in a specialist clinic than in a general clinic?
question.ur: Ek hi test specialist clinic mein general clinic se zyada durust kyun ho sakta hai?

answer.en: Because the patients differ. In a specialist clinic more people already have the problem (a higher pre-test probability) and the problem is often more severe and clearer. The test's sensitivity and specificity can look different, and the same result changes the odds from a different starting point.
answer.ur: Kyunke patients alag hote hain. Specialist clinic mein zyada logon mein pehle se masla hota hai (zyada pre-test probability) aur masla aksar zyada shadeed aur wazeh hota hai. Test ki sensitivity aur specificity mukhtalif nazar aa sakti hain, aur wohi result alag shuruaati point se chance badalta hai.

beats.patient: A 26-year-old footballer twisted his knee yesterday; it swelled within an hour. The Lachman test is positive; the pivot shift is not possible because of guarding.
beats.assessment: The history of a twist with early swelling already makes an ACL tear likely, and a positive Lachman raises the chance further.
beats.treatment: Treat as a probable ACL tear: protect the knee, arrange imaging and specialist review, and avoid relying on the pivot shift in an awake, guarded patient.
beats.reassess: The MRI confirms an ACL tear, and he starts rehabilitation while waiting for the surgical review.

text.en: **A test never replaces red-flag screening.** A negative special test does not clear a patient who has night pain, weight loss, fever, a past cancer, severe trauma or new neurological signs. Always screen first and refer when the history says so, whatever the tests show.
text.ur: **Test red-flag screening ki jagah nahi leta.** Negative special test us patient ko clear nahi karta jis ko raat ka dard, wazan ghatna, bukhar, purana cancer, shadeed chot ya naye neurological signs hon. Hamesha pehle screen karein aur history kahe to refer karein, chahe tests kuch bhi dikhayein.

summary.en: Sensitivity helps rule out (SnNout) and specificity helps rule in (SpPin); the likelihood ratio tells how much a result moves the odds.
summary.ur: Sensitivity rule out mein (SnNout) aur specificity rule in mein (SpPin) madad deti hai; likelihood ratio batata hai ke result chance ko kitna badalta hai.

summary.en: The pre-test probability from the history matters: the same positive test is worth more when the problem is already likely.
summary.ur: History se pre-test probability ahem hai: wohi positive test tab zyada qeemti hai jab masla pehle se mumkin ho.

summary.en: Combine several tests into a cluster for each question, use decision rules for imaging, and never let a test replace red-flag screening.
summary.ur: Har sawal ke liye kayi tests ko cluster mein milayein, imaging ke liye decision rules istemal karein, aur test ko red-flag screening ki jagah na lene dein.

back.en: A negative result on a highly sensitive test helps to rule the problem out.
back.ur: Bohat sensitive test par negative result masle ko rule out karne mein madad karta hai.

back.en: A positive result on a highly specific test helps to rule the problem in.
back.ur: Bohat specific test par positive result masle ko rule in karne mein madad karta hai.

front.en: Which likelihood ratios change the odds a lot?
front.ur: Kaun se likelihood ratios chance bohat badalte hain?

back.en: A positive LR above about 5 or a negative LR below about 0.2.
back.ur: 5 se zyada positive LR ya 0.2 se kam negative LR.

front.en: Why combine tests into a cluster?
front.ur: Tests ko cluster mein kyun milate hain?

back.en: Several tests that agree move the odds much more than one test, and they cover each other's weaknesses.
back.ur: Kayi tests jo ek hi baat kahein ek test se kahin zyada chance badalte hain, aur ek doosre ki kamzori poori karte hain.

note.en: Practise 55 special tests with their positives and pitfalls.
note.ur: 55 special tests ko unke positives aur pitfalls ke saath practise karein.
